lockup.summary: The company, its officers, directors and holders of nearly all its stock agreed not to sell for 180 days after the prospectus date. The lead underwriters can allow earlier sales in writing but say they have no current plan to.

what: ADARx develops RNA-based medicines, called siRNA therapeutics, to treat a wide range of diseases.
proceeds: It expects about $495.3 million from the offering and a private sale of shares to AbbVie. It plans to spend this on five drug candidates, including about $180.0 million for agazisiran, with the rest for research, working capital and general costs.
risks: It has a short history, has finished no clinical programs and has no approved products, so its future is hard to judge.
It expects large losses for the foreseeable future and may never make a profit.
Even after this offering it will need much more money, which could dilute shareholders or force cuts to its programs.
